summary: Timor-Leste's restoration and conservation pledges include more than two million commercial trees already planted in four municipalities, a conditional target of close to one million trees annually, and a Rai Matak programme seeking over 10 million trees and engaging over 20,000 subsistence farming families over 50 years. Conservation measures target two watersheds, protect at least 10% of combined land and marine areas from extractive activities, and designate 30% of marine areas by 2030. The 2025-2030 agriculture pledge seeks to increase adoption of resilient crops by 60% in targeted communities, especially nutrient-dense foods. Land-cover data show 2,313 km² of forest (15.4%) and 12,368 km² of agriculture (82.6%); tree counts lack area conversions, and the crop target is not stated to cover all agricultural land, so no land-area share can be calculated from the supplied data. Laclo watershed spans about 1,390 km², roughly 9% of land area.
